memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then he had another dream, and he told it to his brothers. 'Listen,' he said, 'I had another dream, and this time the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.' When he told his father as well as his brothers, his father rebuked him and said, 'What is this dream you had? Will your mother and I and your brothers actually come and bow down to the ground before you?'" - Gen 37:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph dreams a second time — now the sun, moon, and eleven stars bow down before him. This dream reaches even higher than the first, seeming to include his own father and mother. It is bold, even startling, and this time even Jacob is troubled. "What is this dream you had?" he rebukes. "Will your mother and I... actually bow down before you?"

Once again, we should hold two things together. The dream was genuinely from God, and it would come true — one day Joseph's whole family would indeed bow before him in Egypt. God was revealing a future no one could yet believe.

Yet Joseph, still young, tells even this dream openly to a family already seething with jealousy. There is a time to speak and a time to keep silent (Eccl 3:7). Some things God shows us are better carried quietly for a season than announced to everyone.

Jacob's rebuke also reminds us that God's plans often sound impossible to those who first hear them. What God promises can seem so far-fetched that even those closest to us struggle to receive it. That does not make it untrue. When God has spoken to your heart about His purposes, do not be discouraged if others cannot see it yet. Hold the promise humbly, and trust the God who gave it to bring it to pass in His time.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has God shown me something others struggle to believe?
2. Do I know when to speak and when to stay silent?
3. Can I hold God's promises humbly while trusting His timing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your promises are sure, even when they sound impossible to others. Give me wisdom about what to share, and help me to hold Your purposes humbly and trust Your timing. Amen.
